target: def Target : Prop := ∀ T : Set Form, Def15 T (neg (ex 1 Def17))
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is the proposition that for every set T of formulas, with no restriction on T (so T may be empty), the formula ¬∃x₁ ∀x₀ (K(¬R₀(x₀,x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁,x₀)) is derivable from T in Def15. Here R₀(a,b) denotes atom 0 a b, and the negation, quantifiers, and biconditional are part of the formula to be derived. A derivation may use members of T and the Def14 axioms, with modus ponens as its only inference rule; it is not required to use any member of T. The Def14 axioms are the closed formulas obtained by prefixing zero or more universal quantifiers to a Def11 formula, together with K applied to any such closed formula."}
translation: Target is the proposition that for every set T of formulas, with no restriction on T (so T may be empty), the formula ¬∃x₁ ∀x₀ (K(¬R₀(x₀,x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁,x₀)) is derivable from T in Def15. Here R₀(a,b) denotes atom 0 a b, and the negation, quantifiers, and biconditional are part of the formula to be derived. A derivation may use members of T and the Def14 axioms, with modus ponens as its only inference rule; it is not required to use any member of T. The Def14 axioms are the closed formulas obtained by prefixing zero or more universal quantifiers to a Def11 formula, together with K applied to any such closed formula.

divergences.description: The target omits the K immediately after ∃e. It refutes ∃e ∀x (K¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)), whereas Reinhardt refutes ∃e K∀x (K¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)). By correctness of K, the known universal implies the universal itself, so the target refutes a weaker assumption and thus makes a stronger claim. The unboxed universal does not supply the known biconditional used in the proof.

judgement.summary: Within the stated fragment, `Def17` has the correct diagonal instance and variable bindings. To match the source, the formula derived from each theory must be `neg (ex 1 (K Def17))`.
